summary: HTTP/3 QPACK amplification allows remote memory exhaustion and CPU stall
description:
### Summary

A remote, unauthenticated peer can exhaust memory or stall a Bun process that uses HTTP/3. A small request can decode to a very large set of headers, and Bun 1.4.3 and earlier do not limit the decoded size.

This is the "Header Accordions" QPACK amplification attack that FoxIO published on October 20, 2026. The write-up lists Bun as affected.

Bun 1.4.4 fixes the bug.

### Details

QPACK is the header compression of HTTP/3. A peer can add one large entry to the dynamic table and then refer to that entry many times, with one byte for each reference. Each reference decodes to a full copy of the entry.

`Bun.serve` advertised a limit of 16 KB for a set of request headers, but it did not enforce the limit. It checked only the size of each single header. It also did not limit the number of fields.

Affected:

- `Bun.serve` with `http3: true`. HTTP/3 is off by default.
- The HTTP/3 client of `fetch`. `fetch` uses HTTP/3 only when you ask for it, with `fetch(url, { protocol: "http3" })` or the `--experimental-http3-fetch` flag. A malicious server can attack the client in the same way.

HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 are not affected by this bug.

Executables built with `bun build --compile` embed the Bun runtime. An executable built with an affected version stays affected until it is rebuilt.

### Impact

Denial of service. No credentials are necessary. In our tests on Bun 1.4.3:

- About 6 MB of traffic made a server with a 2 GB memory limit run out of memory and get killed.
- One request of about 20 KB stalled the server for more than a minute, and other requests were not answered during that time.
- A request of about 530 KB kept the server at 100% CPU, and it answered no other requests.

A handler does not need to read the headers. The work happens before Bun calls the handler.

### Patches

Upgrade to Bun 1.4.4, and rebuild any `bun build --compile` executables with it.

Bun 1.4.4 enforces a limit on the decoded size of a set of headers, counted as in RFC 9114 section 4.2.2, and limits the number of fields (#46392).

This changes behavior for large headers over HTTP/3:

- A `Bun.serve` request over the limit (16 KB by default, set with `--max-http-header-size`) gets a `431` response.
- A much larger request closes the connection.
- `fetch` over HTTP/3 rejects a response with more than 256 KB of headers.

### Workarounds

Do not enable `http3` on a server that untrusted clients can reach, and do not use the HTTP/3 client of `fetch` with untrusted servers. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 are not affected.

### References

- https://foxio.io/blog/header-accordions-qpack-amplification-attacks-against-http-3-servers
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/46475
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46392

summary: Bundled brotli decoder has an out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-111497)
description:
### Summary

Bun bundles Google's brotli library. CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the brotli decoder. The brotli project states that it permits remote code execution. Bun 1.4.3 and earlier bundle an affected version of brotli, and they decode brotli data from untrusted sources.

Bun 1.4.4 updates brotli to 1.2.1, which contains the fix.

This is a bug in the brotli library, not in Bun's own code. Other projects that bundle brotli are affected in the same way. Node.js published fixes on October 21, 2026.

### Details

The bug is in the brotli decoder. Affected versions of brotli are 1.0.3 to 1.2.0, except the fixed releases 1.0.10 and 1.1.1. Bun 1.4.3 bundles brotli 1.2.0.

These Bun APIs pass data to the decoder:

- `fetch`. It sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd` by default and decodes a response with `Content-Encoding: br` automatically. A server that an application connects to can therefore send data to the decoder.
- `node:zlib`, including `brotliDecompress`, `brotliDecompressSync` and `createBrotliDecompress`.
- `DecompressionStream`, with the `brotli` format.

Executables built with `bun build --compile` embed the Bun runtime. An executable built with an affected version stays affected until it is rebuilt.

### Impact

An attacker who can supply brotli data to an affected API can cause an out-of-bounds write in the Bun process. For `fetch`, this includes a malicious server, and an attacker in the network path of an unencrypted connection.

The brotli project states that the bug permits remote code execution. We have not tested an attack against Bun, so we do not know how the impact in Bun compares with the impact in other software. Treat this as a remote code execution risk.

### Patches

Upgrade to Bun 1.4.4, and rebuild any `bun build --compile` executables with it.

Bun 1.4.4 updates brotli from 1.2.0 to 1.2.1 (#46392). Invalid data now fails with the new decoder error `BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH`.

### Workarounds

There is no process-wide workaround for affected versions.

- Pass `decompress: false` to `fetch`. Bun then does not send `Accept-Encoding: br` and does not decode the response. This applies only to that request.
- Do not pass untrusted data to the brotli APIs in `node:zlib` or to `DecompressionStream` with the `brotli` format.

### References

- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46392
- brotli 1.2.1: https://github.com/google/brotli/releases/tag/v1.2.1
- Node.js October 2026 security releases: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases

summary: Bundled root certificates trust compromised eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CAs
description:
### Summary

Bun's bundled root certificates included `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`. Eight eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CAs were revoked for key compromise in October 2026, and the six of them that issue TLS certificates chain to that root. Bun 1.4.3 and earlier accept certificates issued by those intermediates. The private keys have been independently recovered by multiple people and some have been disclosed publicly, so any attacker in the network path can impersonate any TLS server to Bun.

Bun 1.4.4 removes the root from the bundle and rejects any certificate chain that contains one of the eight compromised public keys.

This is a compromise of a certificate authority's keys, not a bug in Bun's certificate validation. Other projects that ship their own trust store were affected in the same way.

### Details

Any TLS client connection that uses Bun's default trust store is affected. That includes `fetch`, `bun install`, `bun add`, `bunx`, `node:https`, `node:tls`, `WebSocket`, `Bun.connect` and `fetch` over HTTP/3.

A TLS server that sets `requestCert: true` without a `ca` also verifies client certificates against the default trust store, so it is affected in the same way.

Bun checks revocation only against a CRL passed in the `crl` option, so the CA's revocation of the intermediates does not protect affected versions by default.

Executables built with `bun build --compile` embed the Bun runtime and its trust store. An executable built with an affected version stays affected until it is rebuilt.

### Impact

An attacker in the network path can present a forged certificate that Bun accepts as valid for any hostname. They can then read and modify the traffic. For `bun install` and `bunx` this includes the packages that are downloaded.

### Patches

Upgrade to Bun 1.4.4, and rebuild any `bun build --compile` executables with it.

Bun 1.4.4 has two changes:

- **Three emSign roots are removed and the bundle is updated to NSS 3.131.1** (#46159, #46300). This removes `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, `emSign Root CA - C1` and `emSign ECC Root CA - C3`. `emSign Root CA - G1` stays in the bundle, as it does in NSS 3.131.1.
- **A chain that contains one of the eight compromised public keys fails with `CERT_REVOKED`** (#46300). The check matches the key rather than the certificate, and it applies whichever root the chain ends at. It therefore also covers cross-signed copies of the intermediates, roots loaded from the system store, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, and a `ca` option. It applies to TLS over TCP, the HTTP/3 client and `node:quic`, and to client certificates that a server verifies. `fetch` over HTTP/3 reports the failure as `HTTP3HandshakeFailed`. The list of keys is the one Node.js, Go and Chrome block.

### Workarounds

There is no process-wide workaround for affected versions.

- `--use-system-ca` and `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` do not help. They add the system's certificates to the bundled ones and do not replace them.
- Updating the operating system's certificates does not help, for the same reason.
- Passing an explicit `ca` (or `tls.ca`) on a connection replaces the default trust store for that connection only. A list that leaves out the emSign roots protects that connection.
- `bun install --cafile <path>` (or `--ca`) does the same for that install. `bunx` does not accept those flags before 1.4.4.
- `cafile` under `[install]` in `bunfig.toml` does the same for `bun install`. In `~/.bunfig.toml` it also applies to `bunx`.

### References

- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46159
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46300
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/46526
- Mozilla incident report: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2083449
- uv: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/security/advisories/GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62
- certifi: https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/security/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2
- Go: CVE-2026-111943
- Rust: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0381.html, https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0382.html, https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0383.html
